result.note: Tests the statute being amended for UPI merchant fees and basic payment-fee facts; the proposed MDR rates and thresholds are skipped because they are still under consideration.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, the Finance Minister tabled amendments in Parliament to create a legal framework for reintroducing a Merchant Discount Rate on UPI transactions. Which Act was being amended?
questions.explain: Nirmala Sitharaman tabled amendments to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act on 4 August 2026 to allow an MDR on UPI. Industry players such as PhonePe and Google Pay argue the zero-fee model cannot cover their infrastructure costs.
questions.source: tabled amendments to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act in parliament on Tuesday

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about digital payment fees in India, as of August 2026:
items: The Merchant Discount Rate is a processing fee that merchants pay to banks and payment service providers.
UPI has been free of merchant fees since 2019.
Regulations cap the Merchant Discount Rate on debit cards at a maximum of 3%.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Debit card fees are capped by regulation at 0.9%. The 3% figure is the level that credit card MDR can reach. UPI's fee-free status since 2019 helped it process transactions worth INR 30 trillion in July 2026.
questions.source: whereas debit card fees are capped by regulations at a maximum of 0.9%
